title: Private deployment: Audit log schema, RBAC v2 proof templates, diagrams & hardening checklist
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, actionable audit/event schema and a set of RBAC v2 proof templates intended for Private deployments. It also contains a pragmatic SIEM/forwarder mapping, an evidence-automation filename convention, a small ASCII network diagram of the recommended trust boundaries, and a checklist for network & mTLS hardening.

Context and goals:
- Make audit events machine-readable and SIEM-friendly with deterministic fields for automated evidence collection.
- Provide RBAC v2 proof artifacts (signed assertions / exportable manifests) that security reviewers can consume during an audit.
- Ensure firewall rules and mTLS validation steps produce verifiable signals that are captured in the audit stream.
- Keep templates small so solutions engineers can adapt them quickly for customer installs.

1) Audit event schema (single-line JSON output, mandatory fields)
We require all infrastructure and control-plane components in Private deployments to emit events conforming to the following canonical schema. The SIEM forwarder normalizes these fields on ingest. Example (compact JSON line):

{"ts":"2025-03-05T19:23:10Z","service":"control-plane.auth","host":"cp-01.private.redwood.example.com","env":"prod-us-west-2","severity":"INFO","event_type":"rbac.grant","actor":"svc:se-payments","actor_id":"svc-7b3a","target":"model-serving/namespace:payments","action":"allow","result":"success","request_id":"req_9f8a7c","trace_id":"trace-4a2b","evidence_refs":"s3://redwood-evidence/prod-us-west-2/2025-03-05/rbac/req_9f8a7c.json","raw":"...optional raw blob..." }

Required fields (short explanation):
- ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp.
- service: logical component (control-plane.auth, runtime.gateway, infra.firewall, mtls.proxy).
- host: FQDN or pod/instance id.
- env: customer environment name/region.
- severity: DEBUG | INFO | WARN | ERROR | CRITICAL.
- event_type: coarse event category (rbac.grant, rbac.revoke, auth.failed, conn.established, conn.blocked, firewall.rule_change, cert.rotate).
- actor: subject performing action (user:alice, svc:billing-worker, role:admin).
- actor_id: stable internal id for actor.
- target: resource acted on (route, model, namespace, firewall-rule-id).
- action: allow | deny | create | delete | update.
- result: success | failure | partial.
- request_id: unique request id emitted by the control plane.
- trace_id: distributed trace identifier.
- evidence_refs: comma-separated list of signed evidence artifact URIs (S3 or internal artefact store).
- raw: optional raw payload (only for debug level).

Optional but recommended fields:
- mtls_peer_cn: when event relates to mTLS connection validate client cert common name.
- firewall_rule_id: when conn.blocked or firewall.rule_change.
- config_hash: SHA256 of the active config used to produce the decision (helps reproduce decisions).

2) SIEM mapping (examples for Splunk/Elastic)
Map the audit fields to SIEM index fields so detection and evidence queries are straightforward. Example mapping:
- ts -> @timestamp
- service -> service.name
- host -> host.name
- env -> tags.environment
- severity -> log.level
- event_type -> event.type
- actor -> actor.name
- actor_id -> actor.id
- target -> target.resource
- action -> event.action
- result -> outcome 
- request_id -> trace.request_id
- trace_id -> trace.id
- evidence_refs -> file.reference

Add parsers on the forwarder to extract mtls_peer_cn, firewall_rule_id, and config_hash into searchable fields.

3) RBAC v2 "proof" export template
Auditors will want a compact, signed artifact proving the state of role bindings at a point in time. We produce a gzipped JSONL (one line per binding) artifact signed with the deployment key. Filename convention: rbav2_bindings.{env}.{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS}.jsonl.sig

Sample JSONL line (not the signature):
{"export_ts":"2025-03-05T19:22:00Z","binding_id":"bind-54e2","role":"model-reader","subjects":"[\"svc:metric-collector\",\"user:alice@acme.com\"]","resources":"[\"namespace:payments\",\"model:llama-7b-v1\"]","conditions":"{\\\"ip_allowlist\\\":\\\"10.0.0.0/24\\\"}","applied_by":"automation:rbac-reconciler","applied_at":"2025-03-05T19:21:44Z" }

Signing: The JSONL is signed using the deployment's attestation key. The .sig file contains a compact JOSE signature and the signing key id. Verifiers should:
- Fetch public key via the deployment's attestation URL (documented in the customer onboarding manifest).
- Verify signature and timestamp window (< 30 days old for routine audits; for incident scoping, use the requested interval).

4) Evidence automation templates (commands & naming)
We expect automation to periodically export: firewall config, iptables dump, active mTLS certs list, RBAC bindings, and control-plane audit tail for the last 24h. Use the following naming convention so evidence automation can correlate artifacts to events:
- S3 prefix: s3://redwood-evidence/{env}/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{artifact_type}/{HHMMSS}-{hostname}-{artifact_type}.{ext}
Examples:
- s3://redwood-evidence/prod-us-west-2/2025/03/05/rbac/192205-cp-01-rbac.jsonl.sig
- s3://redwood-evidence/prod-us-west-2/2025/03/05/firewall/192130-fw-iptables.dump.gz
- s3://redwood-evidence/prod-us-west-2/2025/03/05/mtls/192150-mtls-certs.json

Automation snippets (pseudo-commands):
- export rbav2 bindings: 
  kubectl get rbacv2bindings -A -o jsonl | gzip > /tmp/rbac.jsonl.gz; sign /tmp/rbac.jsonl.gz > /tmp/rbac.jsonl.gz.sig; aws s3 cp /tmp/rbac.jsonl.gz s3://...; aws s3 cp /tmp/rbac.jsonl.gz.sig s3://...
- export iptables: 
  sudo iptables-save | gzip > /tmp/iptables.$(date -u +%H%M%S).gz; aws s3 cp /tmp/iptables.* s3://...
- collect mTLS cert metadata: 
  curl -s http://localhost:15000/mtls/status | jq . > /tmp/mtls-certs.$(date -u +%H%M%S).json; aws s3 cp /tmp/mtls-certs.* s3://...

Important: evidence automation MUST emit a parent manifest (JSON) listing all files, their SHA256, and the signing key id. This parent manifest itself must be signed and pushed to S3 as manifest.{ts}.json.sig.

5) Firewall rule taxonomy and templates
We recommend using a minimal, labeled taxonomy so firewall rule changes are auditable and searchable. Labels: team, purpose, expiry (optional), risk. Rule id format: fw-{team}-{purpose}-{seq}

Example rule (paragraph form): allow internal model traffic from worker pool to GPU subnets over TLS: fw-ml-worker-to-gpu-01
Concrete iptables/nft example (for firewall appliance):
- Description: allow inbound TLS from internal worker pool to runtime serving cluster (nodeport 31000)
- rule_id: fw-ml-worker-to-gpu-01
- match: src 10.10.0.0/20 dst 10.20.1.0/24 tcp dport 31000
- action: ACCEPT
- audit: emit event event_type=firewall.conn_allowed firewall_rule_id=fw-ml-worker-to-gpu-01

Management guidance:
- All changes must be run through CI that validates syntax, produces a preview diff, and emits a firewall.rule_change event signed by the CI system.
- Temporary rules (expiry label present) auto-expire and produce a rule_change event at deletion.

6) mTLS validation and evidence signals
Checklist to validate mTLS in the field and capture evidence:
- Confirm CA chain: collector should fetch the local trust bundle and emit mtls.trust_bundle.hash in the audit stream.
- Validate client certificate CN -> actor mapping: when a TLS handshake completes, runtime must emit event_type=conn.established with mtls_peer_cn present and actor resolved (svc:xxx).
- Handshake failure: emit event_type=auth.failed with failure_reason (expired_cert | wrong_ca | hostname_mismatch). Include raw tls alert code.
- Rotation: cert rotations must emit cert.rotate events with old_cert_fingerprint, new_cert_fingerprint, rotated_by, and rotation_window.

Example event on handshake failure:
{"ts":"2025-03-05T19:20:02Z","service":"mtls.proxy","host":"proxy-01.private.redwood.example.com","env":"prod-us-west-2","severity":"WARN","event_type":"auth.failed","actor":"unknown","failure_reason":"wrong_ca","raw":"tls.alert=42" }

7) Lightweight trust boundary ASCII diagram (useful for onboarding docs)
Legend: B = Bastion/NAT, CP = Private control-plane, RP = runtime pool, FW = firewall appliance, SF = SIEM forwarder

   Internet (customer)
        |    
     [Bastion / VPN] -- (mgmt) ---> [FW] ---+--- [CP (control-plane, private)]
                                            |
                                            +--- [RP (runtime GPU pool, private subnets)]
                                            |      
                                            +--- [SIEM Forwarder (syslog/splunk-uf) -> SF endpoint]

Notes: - All control-plane API endpoints are on private subnets. Bastion/VPN is the only allowed mgmt ingress.
      - FW performs deep inspection and mTLS termination to enforce client authentication.

8) Hardening checklist (actionable steps for onboarding export)
Pre-deployment:
- [ ] Generate deployment attestation keypair and publish public key at attestation URL.
- [ ] Configure audit-forwarder to ship control-plane logs to the SIEM endpoint (TLS + client cert).
- [ ] Enable structured JSON logging for control-plane components.

Runtime config and policies:
- [ ] Enforce RBAC v2 reconciliation every 5 minutes via automation and emit rbac.reconcile events.
- [ ] Require rule_id and labels for all firewall rules; reject unlabeled rules in CI.
- [ ] All mTLS client certs must include subjectAltName with role or svc UID.
- [ ] Configure CA rotation window and automated canary rollout for new trust bundles.

Operational checks and audits:
- [ ] Weekly: validate that evidence automation produced manifests for past 7 days and that signatures verify.
- [ ] Daily: run a quick scan for unexpected open ports in the runtime subnets and emit firewall.conn_blocked events for probes.
- [ ] On any config change: emit a signed manifest referencing changed artifacts (config_hash included).

Forensics & incident runbook pointers:
- If suspect unauthorized access: retrieve rbav2_bindings export for time window +/- 1 hour and verify via signature.
- Pull iptables dump and connection logs from SIEM (query event_type=conn.blocked or conn.established with actor=unknown).
- Verify mTLS cert chain hashes and match handshake events to evidence_refs in audit logs.

9) Example detection queries (SIEM)
- Show RBAC grants in last 24h where actor is not an automation service: event_type=rbac.grant AND actor NOT LIKE "automation:%" | stats count by actor, target
- Failed mTLS handshakes by reason: event_type=auth.failed | stats count by failure_reason
- New firewall rule changes: event_type=firewall.rule_change | table ts, host, firewall_rule_id, applied_by

10) Open design questions (TODOs)
- Do we want to include a verifiable timestamping service (TSA) for long-term evidence retention? (Pros: stronger non-repudiation)
- Standardize on JOSE vs. PGP signatures for export artifacts? (JOSE currently preferred internally)
- Should temporary firewall rules require a second approver if expiry window > 48h?
